column3: the profile contract: admissibility, answerability, and the basis of a particular value
column5: profiles.yaml ranked SOURCES and said nothing about the BASIS of a value. A modern-critical figure reprinted in a Catholic reference work arrived as traditional chronology because of the shelf it stood on, and the rule that actually decided several withdrawals -- that section 4.3's reporting licence is granted to Ussher by name and to nothing else -- existed only as a silence the corpus cited as if it were text.
column6: profiles.yaml carries an `admissibility` block: fifteen named basis classes, seven admissible and eight not; the two-question rule (is the SOURCE admissible, then is the BASIS OF THIS VALUE admissible) asked in that order and BEFORE rank; an `own_voice` clause saying publication context is not a basis; a `preservation` clause saying refusing a basis is not an instruction to delete; and one narrow, named `reporting_exceptions` entry for Ussher whose narrowness is machine-enforced. Plus an `answerability` block making answerable-vs-preserved an axis orthogonal to disposition.

column6: All five ruled, three ways, each on the claim's own recorded basis prose. INADMISSIBLE, preserved, disposition alternate: unit:composition.book-of-nahum.chapters-2-3#0 -> modern-critical, because Souvay names the warrant for the lower limit in the same breath as the limit ("a well-known inscription of Nabonidus") and the upper limit is the Assurbanipal capture of Thebes, so both endpoints of the interval are Assyriological, and the article discards Josephus, Nicephorus and Eutychius on that same ground; event:israel.patriarchs.abram-enters-chanaan#0 -> modern-critical, because the claim's own note already carried the encyclopedia's own attribution of the figure, in another of its own articles, to Professor Sayce "if the chronology of the native Babylonian historians is correct", and the profile names Sayce as outside its one narrow lift; unit:composition.psalm-73#0 -> reported-excluded, because the article does not date it on its own authority but "as Briggs surmises", adopting the modern critical commentary it cites by page a few lines later. ADMISSIBLE, still answerable and still preferred: unit:composition.psalm-82#0 -> traditional-catholic, because there the article names Briggs's dating and REJECTS it, asserting its own reading, and states no method for its year; event:israel.patriarchs.abram-contact-with-egypt-and-elam#0 -> traditional-catholic, because it carries no year at all -- only where the two episodes stand relative to the arrival, which the article grounds in Genesis 12 and Genesis 14. column5: Composition-unit scope is chosen BEFORE answerability, so preserving a narrow unit's last answerable claim leaves that unit winning the scope contest and then answering nothing, and the verse falls to research-pending, whose note reads "no ranked source has been inspected for this locus yet". At Nahum 2:1-3:19 (32 verses) that sentence would have been FALSE: Souvay's "Nahum" was read in full, and the finding is that its bounding argument rests on a basis this profile excludes -- the opposite of a silence, and a different fact from one.
column6: Three loci, three truthful answers, and no verse newly reaches research-pending. NAHUM 2-3 (32 verses): a NEW gaps.yaml row scoped {Nah 2 through 3}, whose reason opens by saying a ranked source WAS inspected, quotes both limits and the Nabonidus warrant, says where the envelope is now held and how to reach it, records that the article assigns no year of writing in any case and that the older traditions that would have supplied one are the very things it discards on the same ground, and ends "This row says that, and it must not be read as saying that nobody looked." A WIDER COMPOSITION UNIT was considered and rejected: a unit with no answerable claim contributes no assertion, so it would fall through to gaps.yaml anyway and would only have hidden the question. PSALM 73 (23 verses): falls to the existing book-scoped Psalter row, whose reason now says what became of the two psalm dates it points at -- Ps 73 preserved and why, Ps 82 untouched and why -- so the row is not read as claiming the psalm was never looked at. GENESIS 12:6-9 (4 verses): falls to the existing book-scoped Genesis row, whose reason enumerates what it catches; 12:6-9 is added to that enumeration AND the row now carries the exception in full, because the sentence that follows the list says the encyclopedia articles "date none of them either" and "Israelites" does date these. Gen 12:5 is unaffected (the call of Abram still answers it), and Gen 12:10-20 and Gen 14 are unaffected (the Egypt/Elam contact stays answerable). The Nahum chapter-1 row's closing sentence, which explained its boundary by the composition unit's assertion, is reworded, because that assertion is now preserved.
